title.narrative: Initiativ för att stimulera privata investeringar mot resurseffektivitet
Initiative to Stimulate Private Investment for Resource Efficiency- InSPIRE

description.narrative: *Detta bidrag klassificeras som ett typ A projekt enligt policymarkören för insatser som syftar till att stödja Team Sweden och den privata sektorn inom konfektions- och textilindustrin i Bangladesh.* InSPIRE är ett initiativ som syftar till att främja en övergång till en mer hållbar textilproduktion genom energieffektivisering och övergång till förnybar energi. Projektet bidrar med gåvomedel till innovativa idéer från de fabriker som är viktiga för sysselsättningen men som inte är de mest moderna och därmed ger upphov till stora utsläpp samt från företag som tillhandahåller energirelaterade tjänster.

*This contribution is tagged as a type A project in terms of the policy marker for contributing to Team Sweden/Private Sector in the ready-made garment/textile sectors in Bangladesh.* InSPIRE is an initiative aimed at promoting a transition to a more sustainable production in the RMG sector through energy efficiency and renewable energy. The project will provide grant funding for innovative ideas to factories that are important for employment opportunities but are not the most modern and thereby give rise to large emissions, as well as companies providing energy-related services.

The InSPIRE programme aims to achieve the following programme goal -
Programme Goal: Contribute to an inclusive, gender-responsive green transition in Bangladeshi RMG sector by advancing the adoption of renewable energy and energy efficiency measures, while strengthening the industry's competitiveness in the global apparel value chain.
The InSPIRE programme aims to achieve two short-term outcomes that enables the achievement of two medium-term outcomes. In line with the programme goal, the outcomes also focus on economic and environmental dimensions, while also integrating gender and social elements
- Short-term Outcome 1: Gender-responsive and socially responsible energy efficiency and renewable energy measures successfully implemented and managed by Tier-2 and Tier-3 RMG factories
- Short-term Outcome 2: ESCOs develop and offer energy efficiency and energy management solutions to Tier-2 and Tier-3 RMG factories
- Medium-term Outcome 1: Reduced reliance on non-renewable energy sources in Tier-2 and Tier-3 RMG factories
- Medium-term Outcome 2: Positive net return on investment from energy efficiency and renewable energy measures for Tier-2 and Tier-3 RMG factories
Short-term Outcome 2 also contributes to Short-term Outcome 1 as ESCOs will serve an additional number of Tier-2 and Tier-3 factories beyond the direct grantees through the programme.
In addition to the short- and medium-term outcomes, the programme is expected to contribute to the following overarching objectives in the climate finance and green transition ecosystem, through the crosscutting KEL component -
a) Gather evidence of potential financial incentives to invest in sustainable energy measures to build an environmentally sustainable, compliant, and competitive RMG industry.
b) Expand the market for technical services and adoption of energy-efficient practices by improving the information flow and connectivity among factories and national and international service and technology providers.
c) Enhance connectivity between factories and green financing institutions, while facilitating effective negotiations to create accessible and practical pathways for sustainable financing.
d) Generate key learnings and best practices that inform future adoption of energy efficiency and renewable energy initiatives among RMG factories.

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
The first year of the InSPIRE project, covering January to December 2025, has established a strong operational and governance foundation that enables measurable change in the RMG sector. The establishment of the Fund Management Team, Investment Committee, and standardised procedures for due diligence, risk assessment, and milestone-based disbursement has created a transparent and accountable framework for project implementation. This operationalization has resulted in factories and grantees engaging with well-defined processes, which has enhanced their compliance with financial and technical requirements and improved the predictability of project outcomes .
A major outcome of the project has been the onboarding and mobilization of renewable energy and energy efficiency interventions across ten factories under Window 1 Batch 1. These interventions, including rooftop solar PV, biomass briquetting, heat recovery, and digital energy management systems, have enabled factories to implement technologies and practices that were previously inaccessible due to financial or technical constraints. The outcome is that these factories are now capable of reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions while achieving cost savings, thereby improving operational competitiveness and sustainability performance .
The InSPIRE project has also achieved important results in knowledge management and sector engagement. Through launch events, workshops, and targeted stakeholder consultations, over 80 participants from factories, brands, ESCOs, and financial institutions have been informed and motivated to adopt energy-efficient practices. As a result, market actors are now more aware of renewable energy and energy efficiency solutions and are increasingly prioritizing these investments in their operational and strategic decision-making. This represents a meaningful shift in industry behavior, indicating that the project is influencing broader adoption patterns beyond the immediate grantee factories .
Capacity development and inclusion have also emerged as significant outcomes. Factories have established project sub-teams with at least 30% representation from women or disadvantaged groups, ensuring inclusive participation in decision-making related to sustainability initiatives. Smaller and Tier-3 factories, previously constrained by limited technical or financial capacity, have demonstrated improved readiness to access green finance, comply with ESG standards, and implement sustainable interventions. This change reflects the programs success in building technical, managerial, and financial capacities among previously underserved actors .
Strategic portfolio design has contributed to systemic change by encouraging integrated and consortium-based interventions. The projects approach of combining smaller and lower-risk technologies with advanced solutions has optimized the investment-to-impact ratio and promoted collaboration among multiple factories within the same corporate group. This has led to improved efficiency, reduced transaction costs, and stronger potential for replication, demonstrating a shift in how factories plan and implement sustainability interventions across the sector .
Unexpected outcomes observed include the identification of strong latent demand for green financing among factories, which exceeded initial expectations. The withdrawal of one Batch 1 applicant due to macroeconomic and political challenges highlighted resilience gaps in certain factories, prompting the design of Window 2 to support smaller and subcontracting factories. These insights have led to adaptive project strategies, ensuring that interventions are better tailored to market realities and that the most vulnerable factories are not excluded from the green transition .
Finally, emerging behavioral changes among actors indicate meaningful impact. Factories and financial institutions are increasingly engaging with blended finance approaches and integrating energy efficiency and renewable energy considerations into operational and investment decisions. The target group is now capable of planning and implementing EE/RE interventions with a higher level of confidence and technical understanding than at the start of the intervention. These changes, both at the factory level and in broader industry practice, illustrate that InSPIRE is contributing to systemic improvements in sustainability and resource efficiency within the Bangladeshi RMG sector .
The Embassy assesses the results of the InSPIRE project for 2025 as being of good quality, demonstrating meaningful outcomes and systemic changes in the RMG sector.
